title: Recording with Wooden Joe and Albert Burbank
summary: Russell recalls a 1945-46 record with Wooden Joe; Francis recalls playing with Burbank and photos at Green Hall.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: He didn't have any teeth when he made this record. No teeth. No teeth at all. Yeah, he's a nice old man. Who was playing the corner?
No, but when I heard him though, he had given up music.
Yeah. That was in 1946 or 45 maybe, forget the year, 45. And he just said he'd like to make a record. So you came by and made a record with Wooden Joe and Albert Burbank. Wooden Joe, yeah.

They got my picture, Albert Burbank, too. I played with him once. Albert Burbank's sheet. There was a bunch of us. They took our picture. Some of them down at the Green Hall. Because Albert told me he had my picture. Which hall was that? It's a Green Hall, way down Gentilly. I don't know that then. There was two people down there taking pictures. I guess they must have worked with you.
I don't remember that hall. I remember one hall way down there on Law Street or something.
I don't know. Yeah, around Law Street, I know you're talking about. Yeah. Must have been the Law Heights Hall. But this is way down Gentilly. You're turning your right. Farther down?
Yeah. No, I never was down.

That fellow with the John took out, I played Albert, big sheet. Slow drag. That's all. That's all. That fellow would get short. There'd be anybody that would get up in the water, you know, in your dress, you see. They'd come get you.
